note: Every business rule and NFR in this Unit's upstream set, mapped to the file that implements or enforces it. Where a control was verified by building the WRONG implementation, the rationale records which tests fired -- that distinction is the evidence, because every defect listed passes a confirmatory test. DEFERRED rows are boundaries with a named owner or a recorded cost decision, not gaps.

coverage.rationale: No role column anywhere; the lens is computed per request. 0002 DROPS the role column U3 carried, so the shape can no longer express a stored role.

Owner carries the subscription fields an administrator may read. No admin surface exists in V1, so nothing enforces the field subset yet -- recorded in security-design A.2 rather than claimed as enforced.
create_batch takes owner_id from the LENS, never a parameter. Verified by injecting an unscoped query: 3 of 4 isolation tests fired.
The partial unique index on (batch_id, student_account_id) WHERE NOT NULL. Without the predicate the second dormant seat in a batch is refused, which is the normal state early in a batch's life.
RosterRow carries display_name from the enrollment and never reaches Profile. The privacy suite's no-Profile-import probe covers the module.
RLS stays enabled and FORCED on profile from 0001; 0002 adds no table holding self-authored data.

BOTH gates gained an allowlist and the token lists were unified. Step 7's observation confirmed the prediction exactly: the database gate reports batch.fee_due_day and nothing else. Step 10's tests distinguish an allowlist from a disabled gate -- an unlisted money-named integer is still reported.
A period is the calendar month; fee_due_day sets only the due date. Verified by injecting a due-date comparison: 3 tests fired, including the one written for it.
generates_for_period: nothing strictly after, the containing period IN FULL. Injecting the prorating version fired 2 tests.
set_inactive_from writes per enrollment. A test asserts the other seat of the same student is untouched.
Clearing the date reactivates the seat, so a teacher who marked the wrong one can undo it.
THE CORRECTION THIS UNIT BRINGS. The guardian subquery reads guardian_account_id, so the enrollment a guardian reaches IS the child's -- the question U3's role column could not answer.

The guardian routes key on the enrollment, and GuardianLens.child_enrollment_id is optional because the first request has not selected a child yet. The child arrives as a path parameter, never a client hint.
list_guardian_children returns seats; a test asserts DISTINCT children, since one child in two batches is two enrollments and one child.
Resolved through guardian_account_id, never through the child. Injecting the child-keyed rule passed 3 of 4 tests and failed exactly the one built to catch it.
Attribution travels with every child row: batch_name is on the response and the string resource pairs it with the teacher.
Inverted rather than deleted. U3 banned every write to owner and enrollment; U4 owns them, so one module is allowlisted explicitly and a test asserts the allowlist holds exactly one entry.
Per-LINK erasure markers. Removal tests BOTH conditions; injecting the null-only check fired 3 of 6 removal tests.
The seed script is DELETED and a test asserts no dangling reference. Its rows are precisely what 0002's fold guard refuses.
Money crosses as a JSON string on both surfaces, asserted on the RAW response text rather than the parsed body.
Responses carry server-computed decisions: status is an enum, not a date for the client to compare.
An unknown status fails loudly rather than defaulting, so a server that added a fourth value cannot render every new seat under a fallback label.
Lens resolution stays ONE query after the correction, held by the existing query-count assertion.
list_batches counts seats in one grouped query rather than one per batch.
The roster's query count is constant in N. Verified by injecting N+1: 4 queries for 2 seats and 27 for 25.
The property is constant-in-N, not minimal: a literal count gets raised rather than investigated the first time a correct change moves it.
Both fixture sizes sit below SQLAlchemy's 500-row chunk boundary, or a correct implementation would fail the test.
Four indexes created and asserted present by name.
The fold guard refuses a batch with a student count other than one, naming the batch and the count.
VERIFIED, not reasoned: after a refusal information_schema is byte-identical and alembic_version still reads 0001. env.py sets no transactional_ddl override, so the Alembic default applies.
downgrade() raises and names the dump. It could reverse the renames but cannot reconstruct which student a deleted guardian row belonged to.
The from-head test SEEDS a claimed enrollment and asserts the VALUE survives. An empty table makes a rename and a drop-and-recreate indistinguishable, and a row count passes against both.
The closed taxonomy still holds; BatchNotFound chooses AuthorizationError with 404 rather than adding a sixth class.
One error envelope, carrying code, retryable and message_key.
No display_name or guardian_phone reaches a log line; enrollments are identified by id.
Enrollments are identified by enrollment_id only.
A refused removal distinguishes claimed from erased by CODE, since the teacher's remedy differs.
No new alert: no U4 operation costs money, loses data irrecoverably, or indicates an attack.
No AuthAuditLog row is written; its closed enum is the mechanism keeping it an authentication log.
Per-row audit of a display_name or guardian_phone edit is NOT implemented. A cost decision with a revisit trigger at U7's first send, recorded as such rather than as a privacy position.
Add-student resolves an existing account by phone under U3's existing unique index.
No server-side cache of lens-scoped data; request-scoped memoization only.
Owner is created lazily; most accounts never own a batch.
The roster is unpaginated and the payload grows linearly. Recorded in scalability-design C as a stated limit rather than a solved problem.
One Postgres instance; no read replica, which would also be an authorization bug for a computed lens.
Batch listing orders newest first and counts seats in one query.
The cache is a read cache and says when it is stale; a Compose test asserts the notice appears only for cached data.
No N+1 in the guardian children query: one join rather than a per-child lookup.
Every route resolves a lens through a dependency returning the scoping value. U4 is the first Unit with an authenticated lensed route, so this is where the Bearer header is first read.

404 for another owner's batch, identical to an invented id. A 403 for one and 404 for the other is an existence oracle; AuthorizationError's Literal widened to include 404 with the reasoning recorded.

THE TEST B3 COULD NOT WRITE. The fixture enrolls the SAME account with two teachers, so a query scoped on the student rather than the owner returns both rows to both and still passes any single-teacher test.
Guardian reachability through guardian_account_id. The child-keyed rule leaks across teachers and passes the happy path.
The teacher-facing key is enrollment_id; no response carries a student account id.
No client-supplied lens hint is trusted: the lens is resolved server-side per request.
Owner's administrator-readable field subset is stated in columns. Nothing enforces it because no admin surface exists.
No U4 module imports or references Profile; RLS makes the fallback fail closed even if written.

New tables are GRANTed to the restricted role explicitly. 0001's GRANT ON ALL TABLES covered only what existed then, so without this the app could not read its own tables -- and they were invisible to the governance gates.

The money gate now looks through anyOf, so a NULLABLE money field typed as a number is caught. fee_amount is nullable by design, so the one shape the project uses for money was the one the gate could not see.
